question: Why did a Gemma 4 MTP budget of 8 give no speedup, and what does splitting the wide lm-head projection recover?
model: Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it UD-Q4_K_XL target, mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q8_0 assistant head, BF16 KV

cause.method: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace of ten verify blocks after a 600-token prompt, production profile, busy milliseconds per forward
cause.explanation: The small-block rowtile kernel serves two to eight rows; above eight the launch falls to the one-block-per-(column, row) kernel, which reads the 262144-row vocabulary matrix once per row.

change: Gemma4Runner launches the lm-head projection of a block wider than eight rows in balanced chunks of at most eight rows. Each row's arithmetic is unchanged.

verify_block_ms_median.method: scratch timing loop: 25 repetitions after a 600-token prompt, first 5 dropped, rewind between repetitions, production profile

row_equality: exact verify bitwise equal to one-token steps at 3, 5, 7 and 9 rows after prompts of 120, 600 and 1100 tokens (72 of 72 rows); tests/test_gpu_gemma4_runner_verify_rows.py adds a twelve-row block on the fixture

public_path.timing_scope: whole public call including prefill of short prompts, 128 greedy tokens; plain call first, then MTP; nothing else running

limitations: Whole-call timing is not isolated decode throughput.
A budget of 4 remains the best setting; the per-row cost of the verify block below nine rows is unchanged by this change.
